A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BalancedDPO and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original experiments and illustrations can be matched across the revised layout and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SD1.5 and SDXL experiments, quantitative comparisons on three datasets, component ablations, and qualitative generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds SD2.1 and SD3-Medium comparisons in Appendix C.1–C.2.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an optional weighted-voting extension, s = sign(sum_k w_k s_k). The evaluated unweighted majority rule, DPO objective, and periodic reference-model updates remain unchanged; the weighted variant is proposed rather than experimentally demonstrated.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Pick-a-Pic and evaluate text-to-image generation on Pick-a-Pic, PartiPrompt, and HPD. The additional backbones and 500-caption PartiPrompts subset change configurations and sample selection, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Tables 5–6 introduce base SD2.1 and base SD3-Medium as comparison models alongside DiffusionDPO. The comparator membership in the original experiments, including all aggregation baselines, remains unchanged; no new competing alignment algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1–C.2 substantially extends the evaluated configurations beyond SD1.5/SDXL to SD2.1 and transformer-based SD3-Medium, with 500 PartiPrompts captions specified for SD3. The original training schedule, four metrics, and best-of-five evaluation procedure are retained.

E4.justification: The aggregation and reference-update ablations, seed-variation examples, and prompt case studies are retained. The new backbone tables add benchmark comparisons; the new metric-bias discussion interprets existing Figure 2 rather than introducing another ablation, sensitivity test, or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report five generation seeds per prompt and the same descriptive score statistics for SD1.5. v2 adds no training-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add four-metric results on two additional backbones. Against DiffusionDPO, BalancedDPO reports HPS/Aesthetic win rates of 53.67%/70.00% on SD2.1 and 58.45%/58.35% on SD3-Medium. These are new-setting results; all original main-table values, appendix score tables, and qualitative images are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds a weighted-consensus definition and an explicit two-scorer gradient-cancellation argument. The original numbered equations remain unchanged, and no formal convergence theorem or proof is added. The new assertion of non-vanishing updates leaves opposing tied votes unresolved.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the sweeping state-of-the-art claim and headline percentage improvements with backbone-specific empirical claims. The introduction explicitly includes SD2.1, and the conclusion adds potential LLM/video applications. Majority-vote alignment and dynamic reference updating remain the central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 newly discusses the magnitude information lost through binarization, interprets reference updates as a moving anchor, and argues that consensus prevents reward hacking and navigates metric tradeoffs. It also extends applicability arguments to transformers and other modalities without corresponding cross-modal experiments.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 specifies batchwise Z-score normalization and unweighted raw-score aggregation for existing baseline rows. v2 also provides a direct prompt-classifier URL. The original hardware, optimization settings, reference-update interval, and code repository remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish reruns.

R1.justification: v2 adds Esser et al. (2024) to support the SD3-Medium experiment. The existing related-work discussion and cited alignment methods are retained; most bibliographic changes concern citation style rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets are rewritten, explanatory paragraphs and baseline-definition lists are added, and the conclusion is extended. Appendices receive lettered labels and author affiliations are added, while the main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column main text with a single-column journal layout, extensively resizes and repositions figures and tables, revises caption/table styling, and adds Tables 5–6. All eleven original figures are retained, including their embedded image content.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone results and baseline details provide useful evidence and documentation. However, the new non-vanishing-gradient claim does not resolve tied opposing votes, and Table 6's hundredth-percent win rates for 500 captions are not reconciled with Appendix D's per-caption win calculation. These uncertainties affect the reliability of the principal additions, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
